name: Xia Shudong
current_role: Chairman & CEO and controlling shareholder, China TransInfo Technology (千方科技, SZ:002373)
profile: Xia Shudong (b. ~1972, Hubei) founded China TransInfo, a Shenzhen-listed provider of smart-transportation and intelligent-security systems for Chinese cities; Alibaba bought a 15% stake in 2019 for 3.6bn yuan. He still chairs the board and in 2025 launched TranXmart (千曙科技), an autonomous-freight trucking subsidiary.
interesting_fact: In 2025 TransInfo spun up TranXmart (千曙科技), an autonomous-driving freight unit whose stated goal is to build China's largest unmanned freight-capacity platform, using hub-to-hub routes tested in Sichuan/Chongqing and new-energy heavy trucks.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was an academic mapmaker: after studying at Chongqing University he earned a 2003 PhD in cartography & GIS at Peking University's Institute of Remote Sensing and GIS, and the company began as Beijing PKU ChinaFront (北大千方), a PKU-linked spin-out.
notes: Contact via TransInfo board-secretary office (securities@ctfo.com). Chongqing University detail per WEF profile (page blocks scraping; seen via search).

name: Roy Richardson
current_role: Life President, Richardson family business (Richardsons, West Midlands property)
profile: Roy Richardson (born c.1930) and his late twin Don founded a Black Country business in 1948, moving from used commercial vehicles into property; they turned the derelict Round Oak Steelworks site into the Merry Hill shopping centre in the 1980s. The family business, now run by his sons, invests in property; Roy is Life President.
interesting_fact: The twins bought 400 acres of the closed Round Oak Steelworks (shut 1982, an enterprise zone) and, inspired by US malls, built Merry Hill in eight phases by 1989, one of Europe's largest shopping centres.
deep_cut_fact: He and Don left school at 14 to work for their father selling used commercial vehicles, often post-war surplus, and did RAF national service together before starting in business in 1948. He was the first businessman made an Honorary Freeman of Sandwell (2018).
notes: Now in his 90s; day-to-day business is run by sons (Lee, Carl, Martyn). Twin Don died 2007. Sandwell freedom: https://www.expressandstar.com/business/standing-ovation-as-dr-roy-richardson-made-honorary-freeman-of-sandwell-with-video-6241724 ; alive status inferred from no death reports and 2025 Rich List coverage naming him head of family.

name: Li Xinyu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Talkweb Information System (拓维信息, SZ:002261); also chairs Kaihong Zhigu (开鸿智谷)
profile: Li Xinyu founded Changsha-based Talkweb in 1996; it listed in Shenzhen in 2008 and grew from mobile value-added and education services into a full-stack Huawei-ecosystem partner (Kunpeng/Ascend servers, AI computing, OpenHarmony OS). He remains chairman and holds ~11.7% of the company.
interesting_fact: Talkweb is a core partner in Huawei's Ascend AI-compute ecosystem and participates in China's 'East Data, West Computing' data-center program, offering chips-to-servers-to-OS-to-apps solutions; in 2026 Li gave a keynote at the OpenAtom open-source ecosystem conference.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Talkweb he worked at the Hunan Provincial Electric Power Bureau, giving up that 'iron rice bowl' state job in 1996 to start the company in Changsha.
notes: Energy/data-center relevant (former power-bureau employee; AI compute and 'East Data West Computing'). Power-bureau detail is from a single eastmoney caifuhao article; not cross-checked elsewhere.

name: Wong Tsu-Hing
current_role: Executive Director & Group General Manager, Dah Sing Financial Holdings (HK:0440); Vice Chairman, MD & Chief Executive, Dah Sing Bank
profile: Harold Tsu-Hing Wong (王祖興, ~56) is the son of chairman David Shou-Yeh Wong, whose family controls Hong Kong's Dah Sing banking group (founded 1947). He joined Dah Sing Bank in 2000, ran Dah Sing Banking Group as CEO 2011-2017 and now heads Dah Sing Bank and is group general manager of the listed holding company.
interesting_fact: Dah Sing is often described as one of the last independent, family-controlled local banks in Hong Kong; the Wong family wealth is listed jointly for Harold and his father David (b. ~1941), who still chairs the group.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer before banking: LLB (Hons) from King's College London and a Harvard MBA, and is a qualified solicitor in both England & Wales and Hong Kong; he sits on the Executive Committee of the Hong Kong Institute of Bankers.
notes: Hurun lists fortune shared with father Wong Shou-Yeh (David Wong). No published IR/press email found; route via Dah Sing Bank corporate communications / company secretary (Richard Tsung-Yung Li).
